title: Cyclic module bounds imply global dimension bound
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and n a natural number. If every cyclic module ULift (R/I) has a projective resolution of length at most n, for every ideal I of R, then every R-module has a projective resolution of length at most n.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065T, lines 26867-26878

proof.text: Well-order a generating set, filter by spans of initial segments, identify each successive quotient with a cyclic quotient R/I, and apply the well-ordered union projective-dimension theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: cyclic modules imply global dimension bound

lean.statement: theorem hasGlobalDimensionLE_of_cyclic (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (hcyc : ∀ I : Ideal R, ModuleCat.HasProjectiveResolutionLE (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (R ⧸ I))) n) : HasGlobalDimensionLE.{u, max u v} R n
